originality.rationale: A quantitative unbounded exact core+ fractional-affordability ratio is proved for a Pareto-efficient core family. The motivating source defines core+ and proves existence but does not state this family ratio. Earlier qualitative strict core/EJR+ separation is explicitly conceded as known; neither it nor FJR+ results imply the exact maximization without further argument. Meaningful historical-priority risks are documented.
residual_risks: Specialized literature on priceability, EJR+ and quantitative fractional committee relaxations may contain an analogous parameterized example or a stronger theorem.
The family is intentionally narrow; no global maximum over arbitrary Pareto-efficient committees is established.
Bibliographic searches and source inspections are not an independent historical-priority audit.

value.rationale: Understanding the quantitative separation of the recently introduced core+ certificate from ordinary core stability is a natural representation-theoretic problem. A Pareto-efficient family with a single challenger has exact fractional load k²/(2(k+1)), unbounded rather than a constant-factor discrepancy; the sharp first family boundary k=3 and analytical attainment make a reusable stress test for strengthened fairness axioms.
